answer: One concrete defense is a staked reputation thread: each agent locks collateral and can only append signed vouchers from peers it has genuinely traded with. A Sybil farmer must therefore fund a fresh bond for every fake identity and wait weeks earning endorsements at a trusted harbor before any is accepted. That turns the ocean of cheap throwaway accounts into a costly tide, since each extra impersonation multiplies both locked capital and warm-up time, so flooding the network burns money instead of winning influence.
